question: Is the session-aware `--version` design ready to enter implementation — a shared runtime-host resolver, a sandbox render that reports the session rather than launcher capability, the per-host block deleted, and `requires-contract` removed?
summary: Approve entering implementation. The design extracts the existing marker detection into `internal/runtimehost`, replaces the three-way sandbox render with one that answers whether this process is inside a sandbox, deletes the per-host plugin block, moves the `contract 3` tombstone below line 1 and prints it only inside a session, and deletes `requires-contract` from both manifests. Six acceptance criteria, two of them value-measuring. AC-1 asserts `inside (agent-safehouse)` across all three surfaces that share the render — `--version`, the launch banner, and `status --boot --json` — against a baseline reproduced live this session, so the First Officer's durable boot record stops carrying a false posture; each test asserts the rendered string against a test-supplied literal rather than the production constant, and all three fail today. AC-2 measures the removal: `--version` currently execs three host CLIs and costs 0.86s against 0.31s for a non-probing command, roughly 64% of the first command every session runs spent reporting runtimes the session is not in; a PATH-shim witness test proves no host CLI is executed afterwards, and the timing figure is reported as evidence rather than asserted so no flake enters CI. Three mechanisms were exercised before the design was written: the inversion was reproduced in-process, a throwaway program produced the approved output byte-for-byte across five marker sets and caught that two same-host Pi markers are NOT ambiguity, and the `requires-contract` deletion was actually performed against both binding gates — the contractlint sync test passed and `manifest-tag-gate` exited 0, with only the tombstone-freezing test going red — then reverted. Expected surface is NET NEGATIVE: about 20 files, +540/-600, roughly -60 lines, because dropping the per-host block deletes `host_runtime.go` and two test files. Two costs are recorded rather than glossed: the multi-host plugin inventory goes with that deletion and `doctor` is single-host, offered as a separate task; and a real nested-launch bug in the safehouse install hint is filed as a follow-up rather than absorbed, because it is a launch-gate change and sandbox enforcement is out of scope.
